title: Intelligent Nonlocal Nanomechanics
short: Non-classical continuum theories meet machine learning.
vision: A next-generation modeling framework in which non-classical continuum theories — nonlocal, strain-gradient, couple-stress and Gurtin–Murdoch surface elasticity — are combined with machine learning and physics-informed neural networks for fast prediction, inverse design and uncertainty quantification of nanostructure instability and vibration.
questions: Can PINNs solve high-order nonlinear nonlocal beam/plate equations without a large pre-computed dataset?; How does a fractional-order derivative change the predicted dynamics of viscoelastic nanobeams?; How can uncertainty in the length-scale parameter be propagated into pull-in prediction with Gaussian processes?; Does a surrogate trained on one geometry generalize to unseen geometries?
methods: Eringen & stress-driven nonlocal models; Modified strain-gradient & consistent couple-stress theories; Gurtin–Murdoch surface elasticity; Fractional calculus (Caputo); PINN; Gaussian-process regression; GDQ; Latin-hypercube / Sobol sampling
tools: MATLAB; Python (PyTorch / TensorFlow); DeepXDE; scikit-learn; COMSOL / ABAQUS
journals: Applied Mathematical Modelling; Engineering with Computers; Thin-Walled Structures; Composite Structures; Archive of Applied Mechanics

title: Micro/Nano Robotics with Compliant Mechanisms & Metamaterials
short: From nano-tweezer stability to complete micro-robotic systems.
vision: Moving from static stability analysis of nano-tweezers and nano-pincers toward integrated micro/nano-robotic systems in which metamaterial micro-structure and compliant mechanisms act simultaneously as structure, actuator and sensor.
questions: How can an optimal topology deliver large stroke, sufficient gripping force and nanometre positioning at the same time?; How does an auxetic micro-structure change the electromechanical stability of a nano-actuator under van der Waals / Casimir forces?; Is the pseudo-rigid-body model accurate enough at the nano-scale or is a full continuum model required?; Can topological phase transitions of folded structures be used as a sensing mechanism?
methods: Pseudo-rigid-body model (PRBM); Geometrically nonlinear beams with surface effects; Micropolar / Cosserat elasticity; Topology optimization (SIMP / level-set); Electrostatic + vdW / Casimir coupling
tools: ANSYS / ABAQUS; COMSOL Multiphysics; MATLAB / Simulink; SolidWorks
journals: Mechanism and Machine Theory; Sensors and Actuators A; Journal of Sound and Vibration; International Journal of Mechanical Sciences; Microsystem Technologies

title: Nonlinear Energy Harvesting from Micro/Nano Resonators
short: Bistability and size effects for self-powered sensors.
vision: Using nonlinear phenomena — bistability, parametric resonance and multi-mode coupling — together with size effects to build micro/nano energy harvesters that convert ambient vibration efficiently over a wide frequency band, for self-powered wireless sensors and IoT.
questions: How can bistability widen the effective bandwidth without a large loss of output power?; How much do Casimir / van der Waals forces shift the resonance of sub-micron-gap harvesters?; Can a combined electrostatic–triboelectric transducer outperform a single mechanism?; How does the optimal geometry with Gurtin–Murdoch surface effects deviate from classical predictions?
methods: Coupled piezoelectric Euler–Bernoulli beam; Duffing oscillator; Harmonic balance; Multiple scales; Bifurcation analysis & Poincaré maps; Coupled electromechanical FEM
journals: Nano Energy; Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing; Journal of Intelligent Material Systems and Structures; Smart Materials and Structures; Micromachines

title: 2D-Material NEMS Resonators
short: Graphene and MXene membranes — modeling branch.
vision: Extending non-classical continuum modeling — so far applied mainly to nanowires and nanotubes — to membrane resonators made of next-generation 2D materials such as multilayer graphene and MXene, with a focus on mechanical and electromechanical modeling.
questions: How does pre-tension of a graphene membrane affect natural frequencies and pull-in under electrostatic load?; How accurately can a Gurtin–Murdoch bilayer model predict the stability of anisotropic MXene-based sensors?; How does a graphene/MXene bilayer resonator differ dynamically from a single-material one?
methods: Pre-tensioned membrane equation with nonlinear electrostatics; Anisotropic Gurtin–Murdoch bilayer model; Stress-driven nonlocal plate theory; Galerkin & GDQ discretization
journals: 2D Materials; Nanoscale; Physica E; Journal of Applied Physics; Microsystem Technologies

title: Intelligent Control & Digital Twins of Micro/Nano Systems
short: From robust control to data-driven control and real-time twins.
vision: Evolving the lab's robust, QFT and fuzzy control work toward data-driven control and digital-twin architectures for real-time monitoring, fault prediction and optimization of micro/nano electromechanical systems.
questions: Can a reinforcement-learning controller stabilize a nano-positioner beyond pull-in without an exact model?; How can a light yet accurate reduced-order model be extracted for a real-time resonator twin?; Which surrogate (MLP / GP / PINN) gives the best accuracy–speed trade-off for multi-objective actuator optimization?
methods: Nonlinear state-space models; Reinforcement learning (PPO / DDPG); Proper orthogonal decomposition / ROM; MLP & GP surrogates; NSGA-II; QFT & fuzzy control
tools: MATLAB / Simulink (RL Toolbox); Python (Stable-Baselines3 / PyTorch); COMSOL / ANSYS
journals: ISA Transactions; Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing; IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics; Control Engineering Practice; Microsystems & Nanoengineering
